title: Invincible
synopsis: You're the strongest person on Earth this week. The Viltrumites are watching, your father is back in your inbox, and you have an econ midterm at 9 a.m. Try not to bleed on the textbook.

nodes.text: Your phone explodes — a literal explosion, in the next county; figuratively, your phone — and your professor reminds you the midterm is at nine. You're wearing flannel pants and have a black eye from yesterday. The distance between The Explosion and Mid-Air Studying begins with the choice between “Take the call and skip the test” and “Try to do both somehow.”

choices.text: Take the call and skip the test
choices.consequence: You choose to take the call and skip the test. By The Explosion, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Try to do both somehow
choices.consequence: Optimism is a kind of strategy. You choose to try to do both somehow. By Mid-Air Studying, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: It's a familiar villain — Titan, who hates his name — robbing a federal vault for what he insists are honest reasons. A man yells at him about labor rights. The vault yells back electronically. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Knock Titan out fast and clean
choices.consequence: Speed reduces collateral. You knock Titan out fast and clean. The route to Eve, Calling opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Talk to Titan first
choices.consequence: Some villains are also problems. You choose to talk to Titan first. By Mom, Texting, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: You're a hundred feet up reading econ notes off your phone. A pigeon hits you in the face. The notes get worse from here. The distance between Eve, Calling and Mom, Texting begins with the choice between “Fly to campus first” and “Tutor yourself by saving someone who knows econ.”

choices.text: Fly to campus first
choices.consequence: Take the test, then save the city. You fly to campus first. The route to Eve, Calling opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Tutor yourself by saving someone who knows econ
choices.consequence: You choose to tutor yourself by saving someone who knows econ. By Mom, Texting, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Your girlfriend Eve is on the line, in her own crisis — a refugee camp under threat from a warlord whose helicopters her energy fields can't politely stop forever. She wants backup, not advice. “Promise her you'll be there in twenty minutes” opens the route to The Refugee Camp. “Send the Guardians instead” changes the terms and carries you toward The Guardians.

choices.text: Promise her you'll be there in twenty minutes
choices.consequence: Honor the relationship first. You choose to promise her you'll be there in twenty minutes. By The Refugee Camp, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Send the Guardians instead
choices.consequence: Triage is a love language. You commit to send the Guardians instead. It buys momentum toward The Guardians and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Mom: 'Dinner Sunday. Please. Your sister is asking. PS your Dad emailed me again.' The Dad in question is Nolan, who once tried to kill you, who lives, when he lives, off-planet. Choose “Reply 'I'll be there'” and The Refugee Camp comes into view; choose “Delete the email-about-Dad screenshot before reading” and the road bends toward The Guardians.

choices.text: Reply 'I'll be there'
choices.consequence: Family first, family always. You reply 'I'll be there'. The route to The Refugee Camp opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Delete the email-about-Dad screenshot before reading
choices.consequence: Some emotional triage is preemptive. You delete the email-about-Dad screenshot before reading. The route to The Guardians opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: You arrive with Eve as four helicopters lift off. She is exhausted and brilliant. The warlord is shouting demands; the camp's elder is, somehow, also shouting demands at the warlord. You have ninety seconds. The distance between Cecil's Call and Amber, Coffee begins with the choice between “Disable the helicopters non-lethally” and “Take the warlord directly and remove him.”

choices.text: Disable the helicopters non-lethally
choices.consequence: Restraint is a discipline. You choose to disable the helicopters non-lethally. By Cecil's Call, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Take the warlord directly and remove him
choices.consequence: Solve the problem, not the helicopters. You choose to take the warlord directly and remove him. By Amber, Coffee, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Robot, ever-tense, calls back. Two of the Guardians are out on Mars-related business. The team is thin. He suggests you 'prioritize ruthlessly.' He always says that. You always hate it. “Send Robot to Eve, you take the vault” opens the route to Cecil's Call. “Send Robot to the vault, you take Eve” changes the terms and carries you toward Amber, Coffee.

choices.text: Send Robot to Eve, you take the vault
choices.consequence: Trade routes that fit each strength. You choose to send Robot to Eve, you take the vault. By Cecil's Call, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Send Robot to the vault, you take Eve
choices.consequence: Personal over professional. You send Robot to the vault, you take Eve. The route to Amber, Coffee opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Cecil from the GDA grabs your comm. 'Viltrumite ship just blinked into orbit,' he says. 'It hasn't done anything yet.' He pauses, in the way Cecil pauses. You are unlikely to keep all three. The distance between Orbit and Mom and the Sister begins with the choice between “Fly to orbit immediately” and “Stay grounded until you know more.”

choices.text: Fly to orbit immediately
choices.consequence: You commit to fly to orbit immediately. It buys momentum toward Orbit and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Stay grounded until you know more
choices.consequence: Don't pop the bubble until you have to. You stay grounded until you know more. The route to Mom and the Sister opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Your ex Amber appears outside the lecture hall with two coffees and a small kind smile. 'I heard about Tuesday,' she says. 'I just wanted to make sure you're still here.' It's the kindest sentence anyone has said this week.

choices.text: Take the coffee and be honest about everything
choices.consequence: Decency to your past selves. You take the coffee and be honest about everything. The route to Orbit opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Smile, thank her, and keep moving
choices.consequence: Boundaries are also love. You choose to smile, thank her, and keep moving. By Mom and the Sister, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: The Viltrumite ship hangs over Earth like a quiet threat. The hatch opens. It is not your father. It is Lucan, a Viltrumite governor with the smile of a person who has never been told no on a planetary scale.

choices.text: Pretend to negotiate
choices.consequence: You pretend to negotiate. The route to Nolan, Probably opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Hit him first
choices.consequence: Speed is sometimes courtesy. You commit to hit him first. It buys momentum toward Damien, Anvil-Brained and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: You make it to Sunday dinner late, bruised, in time for dessert. Your little sister hugs your leg and refuses to let go. Mom, calmly, asks if you ate. Family is a planet with its own gravity. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Tell Mom everything about Nolan
choices.consequence: Don't carry her in the dark. You tell Mom everything about Nolan. The route to Nolan, Probably opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Eat the pie and say nothing
choices.consequence: Some weeks, dinner is the win. You eat the pie and say nothing. The route to Damien, Anvil-Brained opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Nolan finally drops you an encrypted note: he's hiding from Viltrum on a backwater world. He needs you to come retrieve a device he stole from Lucan. The device might save Earth. It might also be a test. With Nolan, it's always both.

choices.text: Go fetch the device
choices.consequence: Risk one trip for a planet. You commit to go fetch the device. It buys momentum toward Allen and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Refuse and force him to come to you
choices.consequence: You refuse and force him to come to you. The route to Atom Eve, Tired opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: A villain you haven't seen in two seasons rampages through midtown for reasons he refuses to explain. He is, frankly, having a bad mental-health day. You can tell. To choose “Talk him down” means meeting Allen; “Take him to Dr. Singh — the doctor, not the experiment” sends you toward Atom Eve, Tired instead.

choices.text: Talk him down
choices.consequence: Even punching has limits. You choose to talk him down. By Allen, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Take him to Dr. Singh — the doctor, not the experiment
choices.consequence: Better tools than fists. You commit to take him to Dr. Singh — the doctor, not the experiment. It buys momentum toward Atom Eve, Tired and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Allen the Alien drops in for tacos and bad news. The Coalition of Planets is, again, asking Earth to take a side. Eve, beside you, is too tired to roll her eyes. Allen has, somehow, brought salsa.

choices.text: Say yes to the Coalition formally
choices.consequence: Pick a side before sides pick you. You commit to say yes to the Coalition formally. It buys momentum toward Lucan, Returning and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Hold out for a better deal
choices.consequence: Diplomacy is also leverage. You commit to hold out for a better deal. It buys momentum toward Mark, Honest and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Eve sits down on the curb and admits, quietly, that she doesn't know if she wants to be Atom Eve anymore. The world is loud, the work doesn't end, and her energy doesn't recharge as fast as it used to.

choices.text: Tell her you'll take her shift
choices.consequence: You commit to tell her you'll take her shift. It buys momentum toward Lucan, Returning and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Tell her she should rest as long as she needs
choices.consequence: Real care includes time off. You commit to tell her she should rest as long as she needs. It buys momentum toward Mark, Honest and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Lucan comes back with a fleet. He does not, in the conventional sense, ask permission. He addresses the planet through every TV and phone at once and announces a 'transition.' Cecil curses fluently for thirty seconds.

choices.text: Take the fight to him in orbit
choices.consequence: Where his power is loudest, his ego is loudest too. You commit to take the fight to him in orbit. It buys momentum toward The Big Fight and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Trap him on the ground with friends
choices.consequence: Numbers level the strength gap. You trap him on the ground with friends. The route to The Quiet Win opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Late at night you write, in a notebook nobody else will read, a list of who you owe an apology to, an explanation to, a sandwich to. The list is long. You go to bed planning to start at the top in the morning.

choices.text: Start with Eve in the morning
choices.consequence: You commit to start with Eve in the morning. It buys momentum toward The Big Fight and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Start with Amber in the morning
choices.consequence: You start with Amber in the morning. The route to The Quiet Win opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: A skyscraper folds slowly under your back. Lucan smiles even as you punch him. He does not, you realize, want to win this fight. He wants to teach you what 'losing' costs. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Refuse to play that lesson
choices.consequence: You choose to refuse to play that lesson. By Nolan, Showing Up, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Take the hit so he overextends
choices.consequence: Old technique, new villain. You take the hit so he overextends. The route to Graduation opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: You and Robot and Eve and three reformed-ish villains pin Lucan in a containment field of Robot's design while Cecil's people negotiate. Nobody dies today. It is, almost, anticlimactic. It is, almost, a miracle. Choose “Bask in the quiet for a beat” and Nolan, Showing Up comes into view; choose “Pivot immediately to the next problem” and the road bends toward Graduation.

choices.text: Bask in the quiet for a beat
choices.consequence: You choose to bask in the quiet for a beat. By Nolan, Showing Up, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Pivot immediately to the next problem
choices.consequence: There is always a next problem. You commit to pivot immediately to the next problem. It buys momentum toward Graduation and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Mid-fight or mid-quiet, depending, your father lands. He is older. He is, apparently, on your side this time. He doesn't apologize. He never does. He helps, and that, this time, is enough. Choose “Let him stay for dinner with Mom” and Sunday Dinner comes into view; choose “Tell him to go after the fight” and the road bends toward The Line You Draw.

choices.text: Let him stay for dinner with Mom
choices.consequence: Healing happens at tables. You let him stay for dinner with Mom. The route to Sunday Dinner opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Tell him to go after the fight
choices.consequence: Forgiveness is not amnesia. You commit to tell him to go after the fight. It buys momentum toward The Line You Draw and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Months later, somehow, you graduate college. Your mom cries. Eve is in the audience. Cecil is in the audience and pretending he isn't. Your name is read off a list. The list does not say Invincible. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Take the photo as Mark
choices.consequence: You commit to take the photo as Mark. It buys momentum toward Mark and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Skip the photo and patrol
choices.consequence: There's always something to do. You commit to skip the photo and patrol. It buys momentum toward Invincible, Always and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Nolan, terribly, attends Sunday dinner. Your sister stares. Mom is courteous. You learn that 'family' is a verb you do under fluorescents with too many plates. It is messy. It is yours. You like it. You are unlikely to keep all three.
You tell Nolan he can help the world and stay out of your house. He nods, almost proud. You sleep, for the first time in weeks, without dreaming of him. Some boundaries are kindnesses to yourself.

You become someone the news doesn't always know about. You take Eve to brunch on Saturdays. You teach your sister to ride a bike. You still save the world. You also live in it. The road into Mark began with “Take the photo as Mark” in Graduation; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You patrol, you train, you keep watch. It is who you are. It costs you some birthdays. You are okay with that, mostly. Eve is, mostly, okay with that. 'Mostly' is, in this line of work, a long marriage.
